text.p: Owens Corning launched its System Thinking business strategy Wednesday, integrating the company's leadership in the building materials industry with a system-oriented approach to product development, customer service, business operations and growth strategies.
"System Thinking formalizes a process we began four years ago," says chief executive Glen Hiner told a news conference.
"It strengthens our position as the global materials leader and propels us toward our $5 billion, 1999 sales goal."

He said the company's first application of the strategy, called System Thinking for the Home, is designed to change the building materials and home improvement industries by transforming the way homeowners think about, maintain and improve their homes.

"System Thinking for the Home delivers what 85 percent of U.S. homeowners say they want -- project-oriented solutions, credible information and high-quality products that provide value, peace-of-mind and an improved quality of life," says Hiner.

The company said System Thinking for the Home features four product systems -- insulating, roofing, sound control and low-maintenance exterior -- each comprised of products designed to work together to create a building envelope.
The system approach also provides the information and knowledge homeowners need to understand how their home works in order to better plan and manage home building, remodeling and repair projects.
With the approach, Owens Corning estimates its building materials division will grow 8 percent per year over the next five years while the industry grows at 2 to 3 percent a year.

"We researched the process that homeowners and construction professionals follow on home building and improvement projects," says David T. Brown, president of Owens Corning's Building Materials Sales and Distribution.

"While we've traditionally focused only on how they purchase and install products, we have the knowledge and resources at hand to help homeowners and professionals understand and manage the project from start to finish.

While Owens Corning is the leading company in the insulation and roofing markets, Brown said, the new approach allows the company to expand its scope to compete in the $100 billion home improvement and building materials market, where it can aggressively build share, grow in new categories and generate additional sales.

"There are tremendous growth opportunities in the home building and improvement markets and we have recast the way we do business to take full advantage of them," said Brown. "The home improvement market tends to be relatively consistent, not cyclical, which will allow us to grow through economic downturns."
Owens Corning said it kicks off System Thinking for the Home with a national advertising campaign that debuts this week in news and home magazines and on prime time television.
Brown declined to discuss the amount to be spent on advertising, saying only it would be in the millions and noting this would be the company's largest campaign ever.
